newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end lower in moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end lower in moderate volume.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed lower in moderate pre-holiday trading.
Much of the selling was late in the session as traders balanced accounts ahead of Wednesday's Christmas holiday. CME markets will be closed Wednesday but will reopen Thursday.

Lumber futures traded higher during the session amid talk of higher cash prices next week and improved demand after the first of the year. Seasonally, lumber dealers build inventory in January to meet spring building demand.
One trader relayed talk that cash spruce traded Tuesday at $403 per tbf, versus Random Lengths latest cash quote of $392.00.
Lumber futures closed down $2.10 to $0.20 per tbf with January off $1.70 at $398.80.
CME lumber futures will not trade on Wednesday, in observance of the Christmas holiday.
